BUT its authority check differs materially: search_vendor_rates hard-requires evaluate_permission(...,'COM','View') to succeed or it raises, whereas v_active_vendor_rates' own view definition (and the underlying vendor_rate_versions_directory view) gates on app.has_active_tenant_membership(tenant_id) AND NOT app.actor_holds_customer_user_layer(tenant_id) OR app.is_supreme_admin() -- a materially different, likely broader, authority test with no explicit COM:View requirement. Swapping to search_vendor_rates could silently deny this list to any actor with tenant membership but lacking the COM module's View permission who could see it today (or the reverse, if COM:View is actually broader than membership -- not verified either way). Also its ordering (base_amount) and default limit (20, capped 200) differ from the unfiltered vendor_code-ordered browse in the .from() call. Recommend NEEDS_NEW_FUNCTION unless a human confirms COM:View is provably equivalent-or-broader than the view's own authority gate for every affected role.

callSites.readDescription: getShipmentActualCost(client, shipmentOrderId): select * from shipment_actual_costs_directory where shipment_order_id = eq AND is_current = true, .maybeSingle(). callSites.notes: app.shipment_actual_costs_directory is a VIEW (confirmed via pg_get_viewdef) whose masking and row visibility both depend on auth.uid() (RLS session context: WHERE app.can_access_record(auth.uid(), so.tenant_id, so.owner_user_id, app.lead_record_scope_org_unit_ids(so.org_unit_id), NULL) and CASE WHEN app.has_view_actual_cost(tenant_id) THEN ... ELSE NULL for estimated_amount/total_amount, plus cost_masked flag). No app.* function in this DB returns this shape by shipment_order_id (only touch_shipment_actual_costs_row, a trigger helper, and the already-RPC'd list_actual_cost_components / evaluate_actual_cost_variance which target a different id -- actual_cost_id, not shipment_order_id, and return component-level / variance data, not the directory row). A new SECURITY DEFINER app.* function (e.g. app.get_shipment_actual_cost_directory(p_shipment_order_id, p_actor_auth_user_id)) must be authored that reimplements this view's exact can_access_record scoping and has_view_actual_cost masking with the actor passed explicitly (mirroring the sibling functions in the same file), then wrapped in public.*.

callSites.readDescription: getCurrentBillingReadinessEvaluation(client, jobOrderId): select * from billing_readiness_evaluations where job_order_id = eq AND is_current = true, .maybeSingle(). Serves OPS-181 -- the current billing-readiness evaluation for a Job Order (status, blockers, evidence), used to gate/inform billing handoff.
callSites.notes: RLS predicate on app.billing_readiness_evaluations (billing_readiness_evaluations_select_scoped) is app.can_access_record(auth.uid(), jo.tenant_id, jo.owner_user_id, app.lead_record_scope_org_unit_ids(jo.org_unit_id), NULL) via a join to app.job_orders -- again keyed on auth.uid(), not an explicit actor param. No existing app.* function returns a billing_readiness_evaluations row for read purposes: app.evaluate_billing_readiness / app.handoff_billing_readiness / app.override_billing_readiness / app.revoke_billing_readiness_override are all mutations (they do read-then-write internally but are gated on OPS:Edit authority, which is strictly narrower than the SELECT policy's can_access_record -- NOT a substitute for a read call, calling one of these from a read path would also cause unwanted side effects/audit entries). app.get_ops_dashboard_billing_readiness returns an aggregated bucket/job_count shape for a tenant-wide dashboard, not a single job order's full row -- no shape or filter match. A new read-only SECURITY DEFINER function must be authored (e.g. app.get_current_billing_readiness_evaluation(p_job_order_id, p_actor_auth_user_id)) replicating the can_access_record predicate with the actor passed explicitly, then a public.* wrapper.

callSites.notes: Same table/RLS predicate as the row above, but this is a list read (no is_current filter, ordered by version_number). No existing app.* function returns the full version history for this table -- same reasoning as the row above (the evaluate/handoff/override mutation functions are not substitutes). A new function such as app.list_billing_readiness_evaluations(p_job_order_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) returning SETOF app.billing_readiness_evaluations ordered by version_number, replicating the can_access_record check explicitly, would be needed, plus a public.* wrapper. Could plausibly be combined with the getCurrentBillingReadinessEvaluation function above (one list function, caller filters is_current client-side) -- worth flagging to the implementer as a design choice, not something recon should decide.

callSites.readDescription: listBillingReadinessHandoffs(client, jobOrderId): select * from billing_readiness_handoffs where job_order_id = eq, order by handed_off_at descending. Serves OPS-181 -- every Finance handoff ever produced for a Job Order, newest first.
callSites.notes: RLS predicate on app.billing_readiness_handoffs (billing_readiness_handoffs_select_scoped) is the same can_access_record-via-job_orders join pattern, again on auth.uid(). app.handoff_billing_readiness is a mutation (creates a handoff, OPS:Edit-gated, idempotency-keyed) and reads/returns only the single row it just inserted/found by idempotency_key -- it is not a list read and its authority gate (OPS:Edit) is narrower than the SELECT policy, so it cannot be substituted for this list call. No other app.* function returns billing_readiness_handoffs rows for read purposes. A new function (e.g. app.list_billing_readiness_handoffs(p_job_order_id, p_actor_auth_user_id)) replicating the can_access_record predicate explicitly, ordered by handed_off_at desc, plus a public.* wrapper, is needed.

callSites.readDescription: listFinanceCurrencies(client): select * from finance_currencies, order by code ascending. Serves FIN-194 -- the governed currency registry (code, name, etc.), used to populate currency pickers and to validate source/target currency codes before conversion.
callSites.notes: app.finance_currencies carries policy finance_currencies_select_authenticated with qual literally `true` -- any authenticated user can read the whole table, no tenant/authority scoping at all. Despite the comment in the source file claiming 'no RPC needed' (written under the false assumption that a broad RLS policy alone suffices once PostgREST can reach the table), the table is still in schema `app`, which PostgREST cannot see -- so this call fails in production regardless of how permissive the RLS policy is. No app.* function of any name (searched %currenc%) returns finance_currencies rows -- the only currency-named app functions are unrelated (_normalize_vendor_comparison_currency, validate_currency_code, import_reference_currency, a loyalty-reconciliation currency function). Because the RLS predicate is trivial (true for any authenticated user), the new function is simple: e.g. app.list_finance_currencies() returning SETOF app.finance_currencies ordered by code, STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, no actor/authority check needed beyond being SECURITY DEFINER + granted only to authenticated/service_role (never anon) -- still NEEDS_NEW_FUNCTION since nothing existing returns this shape, but the new function itself is low-risk to author.

callSites.readDescription: listFinanceRoundingModes(client): select code, name, description from finance_rounding_modes (no filter/order). callSites.notes: app.finance_rounding_modes carries policy finance_rounding_modes_select_authenticated with qual `true` -- same trivial-RLS situation as finance_currencies above; the blocker is purely the schema-exposure defect, not authority. Searched app schema for %round% -- only app.apply_finance_rounding (a scalar rounding-computation function, not a table read) and app.round_minutes (unrelated) exist; neither returns finance_rounding_modes rows. Also confirmed no public.* function of this name exists (only public.apply_finance_rounding, itself a wrapper for the computation function, not a data read). A new app.list_finance_rounding_modes() returning SETOF app.finance_rounding_modes (or a (code,name,description) record) is needed, STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, plus a public.* wrapper granted to authenticated/service_role.

callSites.readDescription: listFinancePeriodChecklistItems(client, periodId): select * from finance_period_close_checklist_items where period_id = eq, order by item_key ascending. Serves FIN-193 -- the full close-checklist item set for one fiscal period (used alongside the already-RPC'd get_finance_period_close_readiness aggregate).
callSites.notes: RLS predicate on app.finance_period_close_checklist_items (finance_period_close_checklist_items_select_scoped) is `(app.has_active_tenant_membership(p.tenant_id) AND NOT app.actor_holds_customer_user_layer(p.tenant_id)) OR app.is_supreme_admin()` via a join to app.finance_fiscal_periods on period_id -- again relies on auth.uid() implicitly through has_active_tenant_membership()/is_supreme_admin() (both read session context). Searched app schema for %checklist% -- the only close-checklist-relevant function is app.acknowledge_finance_period_checklist_item, which is a mutation (marks one item acknowledged) and is gated more narrowly than a plain read (it presumably requires edit authority on top of tenant membership) -- it also returns/affects a single item, not the full list, so it is not a substitute. No list/get read function exists for this table. A new function e.g. app.list_finance_period_checklist_items(p_period_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) returning SETOF app.finance_period_close_checklist_items ordered by item_key, replicating the tenant-membership-or-supreme-admin predicate explicitly via the period's tenant_id, plus a public.* wrapper, is needed.

callSites.readDescription: getJobProfitability(client, jobOrderId): select * from job_profitability_directory where job_order_id = eq AND is_current = true, .maybeSingle(). No existing app.* function does a paginated global tenants list with exact count, though (searched: no 'list_tenants'/'get_tenants'-style function). Needs a brand-new SECURITY DEFINER function returning (id, slug, name, canonical_status, total_count) rows or an equivalent OUT-param design, ordered by name, offset/limit-paginated, gated so only actual supreme admins can call it meaningfully (the RLS-equivalent check must be done explicitly inside the function since SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS -- i.e. must call app.is_supreme_admin() explicitly and raise/reject for non-supreme-admins, since simply reading app.tenants unconditionally inside a SECURITY DEFINER function would leak every tenant to every authenticated caller). This is the one call site in this cluster where getting the authority check right inside the new function is safety-critical, not just a nice-to-have -- flagging for extra scrutiny during implementation.

Verify with whoever authors it what authority is actually appropriate here.

No app.* function looks up app.job_offers by application_id. There is also no maybeSingle/null-tolerant read anywhere in the job-offer function set -- every offer-related read raises 'offer_not_found' if missing, whereas this page needs 'null is a normal, expected state' (most applications have no offer yet). Needs a new function, e.g. app.get_job_offer_for_application(p_application_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) returning the row or NULL (not raising) with an authority check consistent with app.can_view_job_offer's logic (HRS:View OR an eligible/decided approver on the offer's approval_request_id) -- note this is deliberately less restrictive than plain HRS:View, so the new function should probably delegate to app.can_view_job_offer's logic rather than reinvent it, plus a public.* wrapper. The page's own comment claiming 'app.job_offers itself carries a plain RLS-scoped authenticated SELECT grant... a direct read via the authenticated server client avoids an extra RPC' reflects exactly the schema-exposure defect this recon is about -- that RLS grant is unreachable via PostgREST since schema app is not exposed.

Needs a new function, e.g. app.get_approval_request_step(p_step_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) with an authority gate (likely delegating to something like app.check_approval_request_authority / app.is_eligible_approval_approver, or PRC:View analogous to get_procurement_approval_context_snapshot's own PRC:View check since this page is procurement-scoped), plus a public.* wrapper.

allSites.notes: Verified via information_schema.column_privileges: authenticated's actual SELECT grant on this table is exactly these 14 columns (15 total, webhook_secret_value excluded) -- confirms the TS comment's claim precisely, this is the correct column list to preserve. Needs a new SECURITY DEFINER app.get_third_party_provider_connection(p_tenant_id, p_provider_code) selecting exactly the 14 granted columns and replicating the OR-supreme-admin predicate, + public wrapper -- mirroring the get_third_party_telemetry_reports pattern the file header describes.

allSites.notes: RLS predicate (saved_report_views_select_scoped): `is_supreme_admin() OR (owner_auth_user_id = auth.uid() AND has_active_tenant_membership(tenant_id) AND NOT actor_holds_customer_user_layer(tenant_id)) OR (sharing_scope = 'tenant' AND has_active_tenant_membership(tenant_id) AND NOT actor_holds_customer_user_layer(tenant_id))` -- this is a genuinely more complex, multi-branch visibility rule (owner-only vs tenant-shared vs supreme-admin) that a new function must reproduce exactly, including the auth.uid()-based owner check. Existing app.list_saved_report_views (already correctly used via RPC by the sibling listSavedReportViews function in this same file) encodes an analogous but distinct 'own OR tenant-shared' scope for the LIST case -- checked its body is a list-shaped, paginated (p_limit/p_cursor) function, not a single-row-by-id getter, so it is not directly reusable for this call site's shape (no by-id path, no cursor semantics needed here). All 18/18 columns are fully granted to authenticated. Needs a new SECURITY DEFINER get-by-id function replicating the 3-branch RLS predicate above + public wrapper -- verify its logic against app.saved_report_views_select_scoped's exact SQL (reproduced above) rather than re-deriving it from scratch, since this predicate is easy to get subtly wrong (e.g. omitting the owner-vs-shared distinction).

allSites.readDescription: listSupremeTenants(client, {page, pageSize}): `select id, slug, name, canonical_status, count(*) over() from tenants order by name asc range(from,to)` -- server-paginated (pageSize clamped 1-100) global list of ALL tenants with an exact total row count, for the Supreme Admin portal's tenant list.
allSites.notes: RLS policy tenants_select_own_tenant: `has_active_tenant_membership(id) AND NOT actor_holds_customer_user_layer(id)` -- as the file's own header correctly documents (and as verified directly by reading app.has_active_tenant_membership's body: it returns true whenever app.is_supreme_admin(p_auth_user_id) is true, regardless of tenant), this genuinely does give a Supreme Admin full row-level visibility into every tenant, so semantics are NOT a concern here -- the only defect is the schema-exposure one. No existing app.* function does a paginated global tenants list with exact count, though (searched: no 'list_tenants'/'get_tenants'-style function). Needs a brand-new SECURITY DEFINER function returning (id, slug, name, canonical_status, total_count) rows or an equivalent OUT-param design, ordered by name, offset/limit-paginated, gated so only actual supreme admins can call it meaningfully (the RLS-equivalent check must be done explicitly inside the function since SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS -- i.e. must call app.is_supreme_admin() explicitly and raise/reject for non-supreme-admins, since simply reading app.tenants unconditionally inside a SECURITY DEFINER function would leak every tenant to every authenticated caller). This is the one call site in this cluster where getting the authority check right inside the new function is safety-critical, not just a nice-to-have -- flagging for extra scrutiny during implementation.

The page's own comment ('a plain Supabase read here, mirroring server/queries/document.ts's own disclosed record-scoped filtering left to the caller shape') documents this as a known, still-unfixed gap from the ISS-2026-172(b) files migration, not an oversight I'm inventing.

allSites.readDescription: `.from("org_units").select("id, name, unit_type").eq("tenant_id", access.tenant.id).eq("status", "active")` -- list of active org units for a department/org-unit picker on the employee detail panel (used for lifecycle/transfer actions).
allSites.notes: No app.* function returns a flat list of org units by (tenant_id, status). app.get_org_position_tree returns a org-unit x position cross-join (denormalized, one row per position under each unit, requires HRS:View) and is not a drop-in replacement -- wrong row cardinality (would need dedup) and joins in position data nobody asked for. app.org_unit_ancestor_ids/descendant_ids only walk lineage from one node. This exact `.from("org_units")` pattern is repeated identically (or with one more filter) in 4 more files in this cluster (positions/[positionId], positions/bulk-reassign, positions/page, tickets/page) -- a single new function, e.g. app.list_org_units(p_tenant_id, p_actor_auth_user_id, p_status_filter, p_unit_type_filter), would cover all 5 call sites if given an optional unit_type filter (bulk-reassign additionally filters unit_type='department' and orders by name). Needs its own authority check -- note the 5 call sites span 3 different access-resolution guards (HRIS, Ticketing) so the new function's authority check must not hardcode HRS:View; needs a check that matches 'any active tenant member may see org unit names for a picker', similar in spirit to what each page's own access guard already establishes. Verify with whoever authors it what authority is actually appropriate here.

allSites.readDescription: `.from("job_offers").select("id, application_id, status, approval_status, approval_request_id, current_version_id, record_version").eq("application_id", applicationId).maybeSingle()` -- 'does a job offer exist yet for this application, and if so what's its current status/versions', for the Application Detail page's offer panel. Single row or null.
allSites.notes: Checked app.get_offer_timeline (keyed by p_offer_id, not application_id -- can't be used since the page doesn't yet know the offer id) and app.can_view_job_offer (an internal boolean helper, not a row-returning read). No app.* function looks up app.job_offers by application_id. There is also no maybeSingle/null-tolerant read anywhere in the job-offer function set -- every offer-related read raises 'offer_not_found' if missing, whereas this page needs 'null is a normal, expected state' (most applications have no offer yet). Needs a new function, e.g. app.get_job_offer_for_application(p_application_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) returning the row or NULL (not raising) with an authority check consistent with app.can_view_job_offer's logic (HRS:View OR an eligible/decided approver on the offer's approval_request_id) -- note this is deliberately less restrictive than plain HRS:View, so the new function should probably delegate to app.can_view_job_offer's logic rather than reinvent it, plus a public.* wrapper. The page's own comment claiming 'app.job_offers itself carries a plain RLS-scoped authenticated SELECT grant... a direct read via the authenticated server client avoids an extra RPC' reflects exactly the schema-exposure defect this recon is about -- that RLS grant is unreachable via PostgREST since schema app is not exposed.

allSites.notes: app.list_warehouse_locations(p_warehouse_id, p_actor_auth_user_id, p_parent_id, p_status_filter) lists a location's CHILDREN, not the location itself by id -- calling it with the parent's own parent id and filtering client-side for the matching id would work but is a hack, not a real match, and would require an extra lookup of the parent's own parent_id first (which this page doesn't have). app.get_warehouse_location_deactivation_impact(p_location_id,...) returns a deactivation-impact composite (app.warehouse_location_deactivation_impact), not the plain row. app.resolve_warehouse_location_by_barcode looks up by barcode, not id. No plain 'get one warehouse_location by id' function exists. Needs a new function, e.g. app.get_warehouse_location(p_location_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) returning SETOF app.warehouse_locations (0 or 1 row) or NULL, reusing list_warehouse_locations' own authority chain (warehouse lookup -> has_active_tenant_membership -> OPS:View -> app.can_access_record via lead_record_scope_org_unit_ids on the warehouse's company_org_unit_id), plus a public.* wrapper. Also note `select("*")` here would need to become an explicit column list to match the SECURITY DEFINER function's return columns.

allSites.readDescription: `.from("approval_request_steps").select("*").eq("id", stepId).maybeSingle()` -- fetch the single approval step row (step_order, status) by id, to drive notFound()/error handling and later feed request_id into the snapshot/history RPC calls, and stepRow.step_order/status/id are rendered directly in the decision panel. Single row or null.
allSites.notes: Searched all app.* functions returning app.approval_request_steps: only decide_approval_step / decide_ai_output_approval / decide_automation_rule_publish_approval / escalate_approval_step (all writes that return the row as a side effect of mutating it) and list_pending_approval_steps_for_actor (a filtered list scoped to steps the actor can currently decide -- wrong semantics, this page must also show steps the actor can only VIEW, e.g. after the fact, or steps not assigned to them). No plain read-by-id getter exists. This read currently has NO authority check of its own at all (relies entirely on RLS, which PostgREST can't apply anyway since schema app isn't exposed, and even if it were, in-process the anon/authenticated key path here goes through this exact broken .from() call) -- whoever authors the replacement should add a real check here, not just port the missing-check forward. Needs a new function, e.g. app.get_approval_request_step(p_step_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) with an authority gate (likely delegating to something like app.check_approval_request_authority / app.is_eligible_approval_approver, or PRC:View analogous to get_procurement_approval_context_snapshot's own PRC:View check since this page is procurement-scoped), plus a public.* wrapper.

allSites.readDescription: `.from("approval_requests").select("*").eq("id", stepRow.request_id).maybeSingle()` -- fetch the parent approval request row (status, entity_type) by id, used to guard entity_type is Procurement-governed (else notFound()) and to feed request_id/status into the panel and into getProcurementApprovalContextSnapshot/getApprovalRequestHistory. Single row or null.
allSites.notes: Searched all app.* functions returning app.approval_requests: only cancel_approval_request / request_ai_output_approval / request_approval / request_automation_rule_publish_approval, all writes. No plain read-by-id getter exists. Same 'no authority check today' concern as the sibling approval_request_steps read directly above -- the entity_type-based notFound() gate is a routing decision, not an authorization one, so a real permission check is still owed here. Best paired with the approval_request_steps fix above: a single new function like app.get_approval_step_with_request(p_step_id, p_actor_auth_user_id) returning both the step and its parent request in one call (this page always needs both together and currently does two round trips) would avoid needing two separate new functions, but that's an implementation choice for whoever writes the migration, not something I'm asserting as required. Needs at minimum a public.* wrapper + EXECUTE grant to authenticated once authored.
